data.exact_reserve_text: The Syndicate has experienced a positive run off deviation of GBP 3,031k in the year, predominantly in respect of Property and Accident & Health business (2015: GBP 3,679k, predominantly in respect of Accident & Health business).
data.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate experienced a gross release of GBP 12.891 million in prior year reserves, primarily driven by favourable claims development. This release was predominantly in respect of Property and Accident & Health business. The overall positive run-off deviation suggests that prior estimates for claims incurred were more than sufficient.
raw_causal_phrases: estimates of claims subsequently prove to be insufficient (reserving risk)
IBNR amounts are based on statistical techniques of estimation
The Syndicate has experienced a positive run off deviation

The liabilities established could be significantly lower or higher than the ultimate cost of settling the claims arising. This level of uncertainty varies between the classes of business and the nature of the risk being underwritten and can arise from developments in case reserving for large losses and catastrophes, or from changes in estimates of claims incurred but not reported (IBNR).

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: The prior year development figure of -12.891m is sourced from the 'Claims outstanding' note (Note 6) and 'Technical Provisions' note (Note 16), which explicitly state 'Claims incurred in prior underwriting years' and 'Change in prior year provisions' respectively (Gross columns). The narrative text on page 18 describes a net 'positive run off deviation' of GBP 3.031m, which is different from the gross figure. The gross figure is considered the most direct and explicit prior year development. LOB-specific movements are only mentioned as a net 'positive run off deviation' in the narrative, so gross LOB movements cannot be quantified. The calculated PYD from the gross claims development triangle (-10.776m) is also different from the explicit figure in Note 6 and 16.
